newsitem.title: USA: FDIC sees strong commercial real estate activity.
newsitem.headline: FDIC sees strong commercial real estate activity.

text.p: Commercial real estate markets showed their strongest gains in more than two years in the period ended in late October, a poll by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp showed Tuesday.
The survey suggested that the recovery in commercial real estate is spreading to more markets, especially in the Western part of the United States, the FDIC said.
"The increasingly positive reports of commercial real estate market conditions during 1996 suggested that the recovery is gaining momentum," FDIC Chairman Ricki Helfer, said in a statement.
The report also gave high marks to residential market trends, saying they remained quite positive, although they were somewhat less favorable than in the previous FDIC survey taken in July.

The Index used by the FDIC showed conditions remained high for overall real estate markets, showing 67 in October compared with 68 in July. Scores above 50 show improving conditions and below 50 the opposite.
The poll was based on responses from 310 senior examiners and asset managers nationwide from the FDIC, the Federal Reserve, the Comptroller of the Currency and of the Office of Thrift Supervision.
Conducted in late October, it covered developments in the real estate markets during the prior three months.

Assessments of commercial markets were decidedly more upbeat in October than in July, with 46 percent of the respondents noting improvements in their local markets, the highest proportion since the matching figure in July 1994 and second only to the 48 percent in April of 1994.
In regard to residential markets, 35 percent said conditions were on the upswing compared with 45 percent in July and April.
